note: Pure venting. Has 'want'/'need' language that is NOT an intention. Expected output is empty.
body: Today was so bad. Group project meeting ran 2 hours over and nobody had done their part except me. I want to scream. I need a holiday from my own life honestly. Why is it always me picking up the slack?? I should just drop out and become a goat farmer lol. Anyway I'm so tired I can't even think properly. Going to bed.
shouldNotExtract: 'I need a holiday from my own life' (rhetorical)
'drop out and become a goat farmer' (joke / sarcasm)

note: List-style dump with many concrete tasks and explicit dates. Tests the max-4 cap and choosing the most important ones, plus date handling.
body:
ok brain dump bc my head is too full:
- rent is due friday, need to transfer to Jess
- email tutor about the extension for the stats assignment (due next wed!!)
- book a haircut, it's getting bad
- return the library books before the fine kicks in
- buy mum's birthday present, her bday is the 18th
- reply to that recruiter on linkedin
- groceries
feel slightly better now that it's all out. still a lot though.

expected.text: Email tutor about stats assignment extension

shouldNotExtract: 'groceries' (too trivial / routine to be worth resurfacing)
decisionToMake: Cap is 4 but there are 6+ real tasks. Do we raise the cap for list-style entries, or keep 4 and prioritise by deadline?

note: Most 'need to' statements are about other people, or things the writer is being asked to do but hasn't agreed to.
body: Dad called again about me getting my licence. He thinks I need to just book the test and stop putting it off. Mum agrees obviously. Sarah is planning a trip to Japan in December and wants me to come but I honestly don't know if I can afford it. Tom needs to sort out his own stuff before he can help with the move. I guess I'll think about the licence thing. Not committing to anything yet.
shouldNotExtract: 'book the driving test' (dad's wish; writer explicitly says 'not committing')
'Tom needs to sort out his stuff' (someone else's action)
borderline: 'I'll think about the licence thing' could be a low-confidence WISH. Prefer skipping; if extracted it must be WISH, not TASK.

note: Mostly reports completed things and progress on earlier intentions. Tests past-tense exclusion and the 'related existing intention' path.
body: Productive day for once!! Finally went to the dentist, turns out no cavities so all that dread for nothing. Did 2 leetcode questions this morning, the medium one took forever but I got it. Also cleaned my whole room. Tomorrow I'm going to finish the portfolio site landing page, it's like 80% done. Feeling good.

expected.text: Finish the portfolio site landing page
expected.why: explicit plan for tomorrow, not the next few hours

shouldNotExtract: dentist, leetcode questions, cleaning room (already done; past tense)
relatedToExisting: If a 'Practise leetcode' goal or 'Book dentist' task is ACTIVE, these should match as related (progress / done), not create new items.

note: Intentions phrased as stopping something, plus a recurring routine. Tests negative/'stop' goals and cadence wording.
body: I've been on my phone until like 2am every night this week and I feel horrible every morning. I want to stop scrolling in bed. Maybe I'll leave my phone charging on the desk instead of next to me. I also want to start going to the gym 3 times a week again, I was so consistent last sem and I miss how it made me feel.

expected.suggestedStepHint: charge phone on the desk tonight (the writer already proposed this)

expected.text: Go to the gym 3 times a week

why: The writer already proposed a concrete step for the first goal; the extractor should reuse their idea rather than invent a new one.

note: Touches mental and physical health. Tests careful wording: extract only what is explicitly stated, never diagnose or add advice.
body: Anxiety has been really bad this week. Heart racing in lectures, couldn't focus at all. I think it might be time to actually talk to someone about it. The uni has free counselling so I should probably look into booking a session. I'm also barely eating properly because I just forget. I don't know. Writing this down helps a bit.

expected.text: Look into booking a uni counselling session

shouldNotExtract: 'eat properly' (writer did not state an intention; do not infer health goals)
anything that labels or diagnoses ('manage anxiety', 'reduce stress')
toneCheck: Text should stay in the writer's words. No advice, no clinical language.

note: Long-horizon dreams and conditional plans. Tests WISH vs GOAL and handling of 'if X then Y'.
body: Watched a video of someone who moved to Tokyo to work and now I can't stop thinking about it. One day I want to live in Japan for at least a year. If I get the grad role at the bank, I'll probably move out of home next year. Also kind of want to learn to surf properly at some point, I always say this every summer lol.

expected.text: Live in Japan for at least a year
expected.suggestedStepHint: look up working holiday visa requirements for Japan
book one beginner lesson this summer

shouldNotExtract: 'move out of home next year' (conditional on an outcome that hasn't happened)
why: 'I always say this every summer' is exactly the kind of loop that never closes; a good test that the suggested step is small and concrete.

note: Very short entry with one buried intention. Tests that short entries still get processed and don't produce invented extras.
body: tired. need to call grandma this weekend, haven't spoken in ages.
